findings.title: Missing `key` prop on GrafanaRuleListItem inside rules.map()
findings.body: Inside `rules.map(...)`, the `case 'grafana'` branch now renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` without a `key` prop, while `case 'datasource'` and the `default` branch both pass `key={key}`. The pre-PR code wrapped `GrafanaRuleLoader` with `key={key}`; that key was dropped in the rewrite. This triggers React's "each child in a list should have a unique key prop" warning in production and can cause incorrect list diffing when items are added, removed or reordered. Fix by passing `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

findings.title: Pause/Delete menu items in list view never render even when permission exists
findings.body: `AlertRuleMenu` now computes the abilities as `(ruler ok) || (grafana prom ok)`, with a comment that says this is precisely to support the alert list view where ruler requests are removed. However the actual rendering of Pause and Delete is still gated on a defined `rulerRule`: `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && <MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} .../>}` and `{canDelete && rulerRule && ... onClick={() => handleDelete(rulerRule, ...)}}`. In the list-view flow (`FilterView` → `GrafanaRuleListItem` → `RuleActionsButtons.V2` → `AlertRuleMenu`) `rulerRule` is `undefined`, so even when `canPause`/`canDelete` are correctly `true` via the new grafana-prom path, neither menu item renders. This is an incomplete refactor and a real functional regression for pause/delete of Grafana-managed rules from the list view.

findings.title: Silence drawer in the V2 buttons component cannot open from the list view
findings.body: The Silence drawer is rendered as `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && <SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>}`. In the list-view flow `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule` (no `rule` / `RulerRuleDTO`) to `RuleActionsButtons.V2`, so `rule` is `undefined` and the `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule` type guard returns false. The corresponding Silence menu item inside `AlertRuleMenu` is similarly gated on a defined `rulerRule`, so the user has no path to silence a Grafana rule from the alert list/group view. Either provide an API path that can act on a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` alone, or remove the Silence entry and explicitly document the limitation, before merging.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries a `returnTo` URL parameter (behavior change vs old loader)
findings.body: The deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the rule's href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })`, using the `createReturnTo()` helper, so the detail view could breadcrumb back to the list/folder and persist the navigation context. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem` builds it as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` with no options, dropping `returnTo` entirely. Users entering the rule view from the new list/group view lose the prior back-navigation behavior. If returnTo is no longer needed (because of a new navigation model), say so explicitly and audit other callers; otherwise preserve it here for parity with the previous behavior.

findings.title: Tests do not exercise the V2/list-view abilities path that loses Pause/Delete/Silence
findings.body: All delete/duplicate/edit/per-menu tests in `RulesTable.test.tsx` (and the `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` 'should render correct menu actions' test) drive the abilities through `RulesTable` / `GrafanaGroupLoader`, which still forwards a `RulerRuleDTO` to the menu/buttons. That means the `rulerRule` / `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` rendering gates are still satisfied in those tests, so the regression documented in the AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2 findings is not exercised at all and the menu-item counts happen to pass for the wrong reason. Add a focused test that mounts `GrafanaRuleListItem` (or `RuleActionsButtons.V2`) with only `promRule` set, and assert whether Pause/Silence/Delete should or should not appear — before this is merged, the question is currently unverified.
